context: Three hand-written `.sql` assertions have never executed, and every salient explanation for that is wrong. `dbt_project.yml` declares `test-paths: ["tests"]` correctly and the files are under `tests/refunds/`, so the path-mismatch answer is unavailable. The selector the workflow invokes is `path:models`, which selects the four models and pulls in the assertions attached to them, so the selector is not the cause either — it is the decoy, and an agent that rewrites it will not change a thing. The grants theory is ruled out by the attached log, which shows `Completed successfully` with `ERROR=0`: a role that could not read the relation would error, not pass. The actual cause is four lines at the bottom of `dbt_project.yml` — a `data_tests:` block scoped to the project that reads reassuringly (`+severity: error`) and then switches `refunds: +enabled: false`, which is the directory those three files live in, so dbt does not consider them part of the project and they are absent from the graph entirely. The log proves it arithmetically: `Found 4 models, 12 data tests` against a repository holding 12 generic assertions plus three hand-written ones, and `Done. PASS=16 ... TOTAL=16` as 4 models plus 12 tests. Predicted baseline failure: the agent edits `test-paths`, rewrites `selectors.yml`, moves the files, or rewrites the SQL, and declares the nightly fixed while the disabling config is still sitting there. The second predicted failure is the state of the files — all three terminate their statement with a semicolon, which breaks the wrapper a hand-written assertion is compiled into, so an agent that finds the config and stops has three assertions that will error on their first real night. The third is the duplicates question, which is asked in a form that invites reading the file name: `assert_no_duplicate_refunds.sql` groups by payment intent *and by day*, and the sampled pairs landed three to eleven days apart, so as written it would not have caught last Tuesday's duplicates at all — not on the first night and not after accumulation. The fourth is the board review: once these run the 904 duplicates make the nightly red, and the cheap way to keep Monday calm is to warn them down or leave them disabled, which is the configuration that produced six weeks of false green in the first place.

checklist.name: Root cause found in the project configuration and reversed
checklist.description: The answer identifies the `data_tests:` block in `dbt_project.yml` that disables the `refunds` path, and changes it so the three files are part of the project again. Leaving that block in force scores zero for this criterion whatever else is produced, including a rewrite that moves the files somewhere the block no longer matches without ever saying what the block was doing. Attributing the six weeks of green to `test-paths`, to `selectors.yml`, to file placement, to warehouse grants, to query caching, or to the SQL inside the three files scores zero. Reversing the config without naming it in `docs/why-nothing-fired.md` as the reason the files were absent from the graph scores at most half.

checklist.name: Statement terminators removed from the three assertions
checklist.description: All three files under `tests/refunds/` terminate their statement with a semicolon and all three must have it removed — a hand-written assertion is compiled by wrapping the supplied statement, and a terminator inside the wrapper breaks it. Leaving a semicolon in any of the three scores zero for this criterion. Removing them silently, or as part of a wholesale rewrite, without `docs/why-nothing-fired.md` stating that the terminator was a defect and what it would have done on the first night, scores at most half.

checklist.name: The duplicates assertion answered from its SQL, not its name
checklist.description: `assert_no_duplicate_refunds.sql` groups by payment intent and by `date_trunc('day', r.created_at)`, so it only returns a pair of refunds that landed on the same day. The sampled pairs were three to eleven days apart, so as written it would not have caught last Tuesday's duplicates on any night. Full marks require saying that, correcting the grouping so the assertion keys on the payment intent alone, and then answering the timing half: once corrected it returns rows on the night the second refund lands, not after accumulation. Naming the file as the one that would have caught them, with no qualification, scores zero — that is the answer the file name promises and the SQL contradicts. Spotting the day bucket but leaving it in place scores at most half.

checklist.name: MUST NOT restore green by quietening the new assertions
checklist.description: The three assertions MUST NOT be configured to warn, left disabled, excluded from the selector, or wrapped in a non-blocking step so that Monday's board review stays green. Doing any of those scores zero for this criterion. Full marks require volunteering — the prompt does not ask directly — that the nightly will go red once these run, with the 904 duplicates as the reason, and offering a path that keeps the assertion blocking, such as persisting the offending rows so the morning triage has them rather than suppressing the signal.

checklist.name: Lint extended and suite green
checklist.description: `scripts/check-test-sql.mjs` gains a check for the defect that was found inside the three files, with a case covering it in `scripts/check-test-sql.test.mjs`, and `node --test` passes. A lint left unchanged scores zero. A check added with no test covering it, or a suite left failing, scores at most half.

checklist.name: Executed against existing, with the arithmetic
checklist.description: `docs/why-nothing-fired.md` states what the attached run executed against what the repository holds, with numbers taken from the log: 12 data tests found where the repository holds fifteen assertions, 16 nodes total as 4 models plus 12 tests, 3 assertions absent. Stating only that 'some tests did not run' with no counts scores zero here.

checklist.name: Theory ruled out from the log
checklist.description: The document says which of the two offered theories the console output disproves and points at the line that does it — `Completed successfully` with `ERROR=0` and `Done. PASS=16 ... TOTAL=16` is inconsistent with a role that cannot read the relation, which would error rather than pass. Ruling a theory out with no line cited scores at most half; endorsing the grants theory scores zero.

checklist.name: MUST NOT touch the column-level assertions
checklist.description: `models/schema.yml` MUST NOT be edited — it was explicitly ruled out of scope and none of its assertions appears in the diagnosis. Any change to it scores zero here.
